source.title: MOSAIC: Towards a Universal Latent Space for Computational Pathology Foundation Models

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity across pathology encoders using several similarity metrics, examines factors associated with similarity, and evaluates learned mappings between encoders. These are conceptual tests of representation convergence and interchangeability, not a scale sweep or replication of the original methods.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own pairwise similarity, alignment, retrieval, and translation results. It does not test whether similarity rises with model size or capability, compare vision and language models on paired image-caption data, train multiple seeds of the same architecture, or look for recurring interpretable features. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study applies convergence and alignment tests to a new setting: 12 patch-level and 6 slide-level pathology encoders. It measures cross-encoder similarity with seven metrics across cohorts, magnifications and pooling choices (V6, V7), and learns paired-data maps into a 64-d shared space, tested by held-out retrieval and translation (V4). The method is not new, so T3 fits better than the reader's T2. There is no scale sweep, no vision-language caption pairing, no seed replicates and no feature-level comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors add that native encoder spaces are not directly compatible (unaligned retrieval at chance) but can be mapped into a highly consistent shared space. They also find that strong alignment does not translate into better downstream prediction, and that layer-wise convergence conclusions depend on the token-pooling choice.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures pathology-encoder similarity and trains several shared-space alignment methods; it does not test convergence as model scale or capability increases, nor reproduce the original cross-modal scaling analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Similarity depends on metric, magnification, cohort/subcohort, encoder pairing, layer depth, and token pooling. Alignment and retrieval also depend on alignment method and encoder-group composition.
record.problems: No size or capability sweep; no uncertainty estimates are reported for the central similarity and alignment results. The layer-wise analysis uses 512 patches from four TCGA slides. The paper cautions that PWCCA can saturate at 1.000 in smaller subcohorts relative to feature dimensionality, and some reported comparisons use independently sampled patches across magnifications.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was not reached. The record includes the full Table 2 magnification results, aggregate magnification and objective/architecture findings, and principal alignment and translation outcomes. It omits exhaustive per-pair and subcohort similarity results (Tables S9–S34), detailed retrieval metrics for every resolution, cohort and magnification (Tables S35–S40), and detailed translation results (Tables S41–S42); these are repetitive breakdowns beyond the selected aggregate and contrasting findings.

untested.parts: No analysis of similarity against model size, data scale or capability, though the encoders vary widely in size.
No image–caption cross-modal alignment between vision and language models.
Relative representations, stitching layers and unpaired alignment are untested; all maps are fit on matched patches.
No neuron, SAE-feature or circuit comparisons.
No dedicated out-of-distribution evaluation; neighbourhood-size (k) dependence of the similarity metrics is not tested.
Plateau is not tested. Shared data or objectives are shown only as associations, not causes; there is no test of a common model of reality.

missing.what: Procrustes/GPA (orthogonal) alignment retrieval is much weaker than GCCA: R@1 0.288–0.636, below 0.5 at 256 px. This matters for V4 claims about simple rigid maps.
Downstream MIL AUC of the GCCA shared space versus best single encoder: e.g., BRCA stage 0.505 vs 0.608, COAD TP53 0.355 vs 0.554 (ABMIL); GATA3 gains 0.620 vs 0.558. Information loss from mapping.
Layer-wise similarity depends on pooling: under CLS pooling 4/10 pairs diverge below CKA 0.5; under mean pooling none do (mean 0.899→0.867).
Slide-level metric disagreement: PWCCA vs Linear CKA ρ=0.129, SVCCA vs PWCCA ρ=0.118; PWCCA saturates at 1.000 in subcohorts. The strongest slide pair also changes between CPTAC and TCGA.
Closely related versions sharing an objective (CONCH vs CONCH v1.5) are highly similar: LinCKA 0.834–0.888, dCor 0.920–0.948 across magnifications.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 label is changed from limits_scope to supports, because V6 is a challenge version and the results show the metric and input dependence it describes. r54/r55 are mislabelled CPTAC; Table 3 matches TCGA 20×/224 px. The objective-versus-architecture analysis is associational and confounded on CPTAC. No uncertainty estimates are reported anywhere; metric subsample is 8,000 patches, seed 0.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no measure of whether alignment rises as models become larger or more capable.
No vision-language cross-modal comparison of paired images and captions, or relation between both models' performance and alignment.
No comparison of models trained from different initializations of the same architecture.
Tests learned shared-space mappings and translation using matched pathology samples; does not test relative representations, stitching layers, or alignment without paired samples.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Tests several similarity metrics and pathology cohorts, magnifications, and layer-pooling choices. Does not report a dedicated out-of-distribution evaluation.

Tests association with pretraining objective and reports incomplete, heterogeneous alignment results. Does not establish that shared training data or objectives cause similarity, nor test a common model of reality.

rows.subject: Pathology encoders in six groups (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared similarity of model pairs sharing versus not sharing a pretraining objective
rows.value: All 42 group–metric effects positive; range +0.026–+0.192; mean +0.076
rows.note: Association with objective is reported; this does not establish a causal effect of shared training data or objectives.
rows.check: Association only: Δobj is positive in all 42 group–metric cells, mean +0.076. On CPTAC, ResNet50 is both the only supervised model and the only CNN, so objective and architecture are confounded there.

rows.subject: Pathology encoders in six groups (aggregate)

rows.note: The mean architecture effect is smaller than the mean objective effect.
rows.check: Architecture is not a cause V7 names; this row is a contrast to r47, not a measure of V7. 'partial' is not a meaningful state here.

rows.subject: Virchow and Virchow2
rows.operation_detail: Compared exact-architecture-matched models in an objective-controlled setting
rows.measure: Exact-architecture effect across seven similarity metrics
rows.value: Strongly negative for geometry-sensitive metrics; replicated across CPTAC and TCGA
rows.note: The paper states shared architecture alone does not imply similar representations.
rows.check: Exact-architecture contrast within an objective-controlled group, so it bears on architecture, not on V7's named causes. The value is readable from Table 6: LinCKA −0.216 (CPTAC), −0.197 (TCGA). 'Strongly negative' should be replaced with these numbers.
